title: Plan a prompt kit that keeps one brand look across a whole campaign
scenario: A ceramic-mug shop launches an autumn campaign. You build the prompt kit: the style words, the reference files, the edit, the video start and the checks that must hold for all 24 images and the teaser. Use the exhibit. The shop, the files and the test are made up for this case; the vendor lines are copied from the docs.
exhibit:
BRIEF:
  Brand: Kiln & Co, hand-made ceramic mugs. Campaign: "Autumn Glaze", 3 weeks.
  Deliverables: 24 square social images, and one vertical 16-second teaser with
         sound, made of two 8-second shots.
  Client files: anchor.png (the approved hero image), 8 mug photos (one per
         glaze colour), 4 drawings of the shop's cat mascots, logo.png.
  Client note: "All 24 images must look like one family."

KIT DRAFT (ours):
  Style block v1: "Paper-cut collage illustration, layered teal and coral paper,
         soft shadow between the layers, plain cream background. A speckled mug
         with steam sits on a shelf."
  Every prompt = style block v1 + one subject line.

TEST, POST 2:
  Subject line: "Subject: a paper bag of coffee beans."
  Result: the right look. A bag of beans, and also a speckled mug with steam
         on a shelf behind it.

REQUESTS STILL TO PLAN:
  A  A group shot with the 4 cat drawings and the 8 mug photos as references.
     No style board.
  B  On an OpenAI GPT Image model, change only the glaze of the mug in
     anchor.png, from teal to ochre, with a mask. logo.png and one cat drawing
     go in as extra input images.
  C  (Veo 3.1) Shot 1 of the teaser must begin exactly on anchor.png.
  D  A check of shot 1 and shot 2 before they go to the client. A vision model
     got the first, middle and last frame of each shot and the checklist (mug
     shape, glaze colour, logo, cream background). Its report: all 6 frames pass.

GOOGLE IMAGE DOCS, reference images (table, shortened):
                                 Nano Banana   Nano Banana 2.1   Nano Banana
                                 2 Lite        & Nano Banana 2   Pro
  Objects, high fidelity         up to 14         up to 10      up to 6
  Characters, kept consistent    N/A              up to 4       up to 5
  Style references               N/A              N/A           up to 3
  Also: "Nano Banana models allow you to mix up to 14 reference images."

OPENAI IMAGE DOCS, edit with a mask (line):
  "If you provide multiple input images, the mask will be applied to the first image."

GOOGLE VEO DOCS (lines):
  "Veo uses the input image as the initial frame."
  "Veo 3.1 now accepts up to 3 reference images to guide your generated video's
   content. Provide images of a person, character, or product to preserve the
   subject's appearance in the output video."
  Veo 3.1 can also take a first frame and a last frame.

questions.prompt: Post 2 shows a mug that its subject line never asked for. Which change to the kit fixes it?

options.text: Write the style block again in new words for each post, so every post gets a fresh description of the scene.
options.explanation: New words for each post make the look drift. The same block should open every prompt. The extra mug comes from one sentence in the block, not from the wording.

options.text: Run post 2 again until a version comes back without the mug, and keep the style block as it is.
options.explanation: The block adds the mug to every prompt. Reruns may hide it once, but the next post will show it again.

options.text: Move the speckled-mug sentence out of the style block and into the subject lines of posts that need one.
options.explanation: Right. A style block holds the look only. The mug is a subject, so it goes in the subject line. Then the bag of beans gets no mug, and the mug posts still get one.

options.text: Lower the quality setting to low, so the model adds fewer extra objects to the picture.
options.explanation: Quality changes detail, speed and cost. It does not remove a sentence from the prompt. The mug is in the block, so it stays.

questions.prompt: Request A needs the 4 cat drawings and the 8 mug photos as references. Which column of the Google table covers it in one request?

options.text: Nano Banana 2.1 & Nano Banana 2: up to 10 object images and up to 4 character images.
options.explanation: Right. The 8 mugs are under 10 objects. The 4 cats equal the 4 characters it allows. Both limits are met, and no style board is needed.

options.text: Nano Banana Pro: it allows up to 5 character images, which is more than the 4 cats that we have.
options.explanation: Pro allows only up to 6 object images, and there are 8 mugs. Its higher character limit does not help.

options.text: Nano Banana 2 Lite: it allows up to 14 object images, which is the most of the three models.
options.explanation: The table lists characters as N/A for this model, so it cannot keep the 4 cats consistent. The object limit alone is not enough.

options.text: Any of the three, because 12 images in total is under the limit of 14 reference images.
options.explanation: The 14 is a total. Each type has its own limit by model, and the limits differ. Pro fails on 8 objects, and Lite lists characters as N/A.

questions.prompt: Request B: you will use a mask, and logo.png and a cat drawing are extra input images. In what order do you send the files?

options.text: Send logo.png first, so the logo stays exact, then anchor.png. Make the mask for logo.png.
options.explanation: The mask is applied to the first image. Then it would be applied to the logo file, not to the mug in anchor.png.

options.text: Send the files in any order. The model finds the image the mask fits by its shape and size.
options.explanation: OpenAI says the mask is applied to the first image. The order decides which image is edited.

options.text: Send anchor.png last, as the newest image, and make the mask for the last file in the list.
options.explanation: The mask is applied to the first image, not the last. A mask made for the last file would land on the wrong picture.

options.text: Send anchor.png first and make the mask for it. Then add logo.png and the cat drawing.
options.explanation: Right. With several input images, the mask applies to the first one. So the picture to edit goes first, and the extras follow.

questions.prompt: Request C: shot 1 must begin exactly on anchor.png. What do you give the video model?

options.text: Describe the hero image in words only. A video model cannot take an image as input.
options.explanation: Veo can take an input image. The docs say it uses that image as the initial frame, which is exactly what you need.

options.text: Give anchor.png as the input image. Veo uses it as the initial frame of the shot.
options.explanation: Right. The docs say Veo uses the input image as the initial frame. That makes the shot begin on the approved image.

options.text: Give anchor.png as a reference image. References keep the subject looking the same in the shot.
options.explanation: References guide the subject's appearance, but the docs say the input image is the one used as the initial frame. A reference does not set where the shot begins.

options.text: Set anchor.png as the last frame, so the shot ends on the approved hero image.
options.explanation: Veo 3.1 can take a last frame, but that sets how the shot ends. The client asked for the shot to begin on the image.

questions.prompt: For request D, what is still missing before the teaser goes to the client?

options.text: Nothing. All 6 frames passed the checklist, so the model has checked the whole teaser.
options.explanation: Six still frames show 6 moments. They cannot show whether the movement looks right, and they carry no sound.

options.text: Ask the vision model whether the clip was made by AI, and add its answer to the report.
options.explanation: Anthropic says Claude cannot tell if an image is AI-made and not to rely on it for that. Our rule takes this to every vision model. You made the clip with AI, so no report line can prove anything.

options.text: A person watches the whole clip, with sound on, for motion and sound, and signs off.
options.explanation: Right. Frames cannot tell you if the motion looks right or the sound fits. The model's pass is a first check, and a person decides.

options.text: Send 12 more frames from each shot to the model. With enough frames, no one needs to watch the clip.
options.explanation: More stills do not play the motion or the sound. The model's pass is a first check, and a person still watches the clip.
